newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas water bonds bill passes budget panel.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas water bonds bill passes budget panel.

text.p: A bill authorizing up to $12 million of additional bonding authority for Arkansas Soil and Water Conservation Commission passed the state legislature's joint budget committee Thursday morning.

"We've got to do it because we are holding up some bond issuance and some construction projects on some water and sewer (systems) in the state of Arkansas," said Rep. Lloyd George, D-27, who introduced the bill to the state's House of Representatives on Feb 5. "We just neglected to anticipate how much expansion the State of Arkansas was going to have."
Arkansas' economy is "the best it has been in the history of the state," George said.
The $12.025 million of added bonding authority is designed to tide the commission over for the remainder of its current fiscal period, which concludes June 30, he said.
"This is an emergency procedure to get them from now to the first of July," George said.
The bill now goes first to Arkansas House floor, and then to the Senate, he said.
"It will be just be a walk through, it will pass," George said. "Then the governor will sign it, and we will have our money."

Jon Sweeney, a soil and water commission deputy director, said the bill also authorizes issuance of up to $24.7 million of the same bonds during the next fiscal biennium, which begins July 1, 1997 and runs to June 30, 1999.
